title: finding(process): a closing keyword in a merged PR body does not close the card in this repo — 29 of 29 measured closes were performed by hand, 0 by a commit, and the same is true of the bare `#N` form
body:
Filed by the `domain:spec` @ objectui execution seat, 2026-09-14T08:48Z, from the post-merge bookkeeping of PR objectui#9470. ⛔ Bare `finding` — no `domain:*`, no priority, no type, no assignee.

## The claim

**A closing keyword in a merged PR body does not close the referenced card in this repository.** Every card close in the measured sample was performed by hand, minutes after the merge, by a person or a bot.

## Measured

Population: **300 closed pull requests** fetched over 3 pages of `/pulls?state=closed&sort=updated`, of which the merged ones were scanned for `(?:Fixes|Closes|Resolves|Fixed|Closed|Resolved)\s+<ref>`. Reading taken 2026-09-14T08:46–08:48Z.

The instrument is the issue **timeline**'s `closed` event, not the issue's `state`. ⭐ That distinction is the whole measurement: a close performed by a landing commit records a `commit_id` on that event; a close performed by a person or a bot records an `actor` and leaves `commit_id` null. `state: closed` alone cannot tell the two apart, which is why counting closed cards proves nothing here.

| spelling | pairs measured | closed BY COMMIT | closed BY ACTOR |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| `Fixes objectui#N` | 3 (all of them) | **0** | **3** |
| `Fixes #N` (bare) | 25 (sampled from 300) | **0** | **25** |
| `Fixes objectstack-ai/objectui#N` | 1 (all of them) | **0** | **1** |

**29 of 29 closed by an actor. Zero by a commit.** The closers are spread across five accounts — `os-tesla`, `baozhoutao`, `os-zhuang`, `os-warren`, `claude[bot]` — so this is not one seat's habit; it is the repository's actual behaviour, already being absorbed by everyone who lands work here.

The specific case that started this, with its timings:

```
PR #9470 merged 2026-09-14T08:43:33Z, body carries  "Fixes objectui#8653."
issue #8653 closed 2026-09-14T08:45:25Z  by claude[bot]  commit_id=None     <- by hand, ~2 min later
PR #9009 merged 2026-09-10T18:52:15Z -> #8623 closed 18:54:52Z by actor, commit_id=None
PR #9007 merged 2026-09-10T18:51:55Z -> #8554 closed 18:55:41Z by actor, commit_id=None
```

## ⭐ Why this costs more than one manual close

It explains a recurring residue rather than being a new one. This seat had recorded, six times over, that `pm:dispatched` is "never auto-stripped by a merged `Fixes`". The label survives because **nothing closed the card** — the close and the `pm:*` strip are the same missing step, not two.

⇒ operationally, for every seat: **a merged closing keyword is not bookkeeping.** The close, the `state_reason: completed`, and the `pm:*` strip are all owed by hand, and a seat that trusts the keyword leaves a closed-in-fact card sitting `open` + `pm:dispatched` on the board, where the next round reads it as live work.

## ⚠️ A hypothesis this card had and DISCARDED — recorded so the next reader does not re-run it

The first reading was n=1: `Fixes objectui#8653` did not close #8653, and `objectui#N` is not one of the two reference forms GitHub documents (`#N` and `owner/repo#N`). The hypothesis wrote itself — *this repo's full-name PM convention silently disables closing keywords*.

⛔ **It is false, and two separate errors produced it:**

1. **The subject sample was contaminated by the measurer.** Widening to 390 merged PRs found 3 `objectui#N` pairs, all `state: closed` — which looked like a refutation, except that one of the three was #8653, *which this seat had hand-closed two minutes earlier*. A census that includes the measurer's own intervention cannot distinguish the mechanism from the measurer.
2. **`state` was the wrong instrument.** Only the timeline's `commit_id` separates an auto-close from a manual one. Switching instruments turned "all three closed, hypothesis refuted" into "all three closed by hand, and so is every control" — a different and much larger finding.

⭐ The control is what settled it: the bare `#N` form, which GitHub certainly does resolve, behaves **identically** — 25 of 25 by actor. So the reference spelling is not the variable, and a card filed on the first hypothesis would have sent someone to rewrite every PR template for nothing.

## ⚠️ NOT measured

- **The cause.** No repository setting, workflow, or merge-queue behaviour was inspected. The merge commit for #9470 demonstrably *does* carry `Fixes objectui#8653.` in its body on `main`, so the keyword reaches the default branch and the close still does not happen. Why is unmeasured, and ⛔ this card asserts no cause.
- Whether a **non-queue** merge in this repo behaves differently — the sample may contain no such merge, and none was isolated.
- 25 of 300 bare-form pairs were sampled, not all 300; the other two spellings were measured exhaustively (3 and 1).
- An earlier pass reported 16 bare-form pairs as `state: None`. Those are unreadable API responses, ⛔ **not** counter-examples, and they are excluded rather than counted either way.
- Whether the sibling repositories behave the same. This reading is objectui-only.

## Dedup

Two phrasings of this subject returned 0. ⚠️ The control is **same-repo and same-instrument but not same-subject**: queries about other CI/tooling subjects in this repo return results (a coverage-gate query returned 12 including objectui#9271; a renderer-cast query returned 4), so the instrument is answering in this repo. On that basis the zero is treated as a reading, ⛔ with the weaker control stated rather than implied.
